MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

WARM UP

Basketball School

TEAM TAG

10 MIN
BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Different groups inside half-court areas.

### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball for dribbling loads.

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided into teams consisting of anywhere between four and 10 players. One team will start as the 'escapers' inside the half-court boundaries, while the other team will start as the 'taggers' and stand in a line on the baseline. When the first tagger runs out and attempts to tag one of the escapers, the coach starts recording time on a stopwatch. The moment an escaper is tagged, they must stand out on the sideline, while the tagger sprints back to hi-five the next tagger who can start to run out. Time stops when all the escapers are tagged. Both teams then change roles, with the other team attempting to beat the first team's time to win the game.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play in a smaller space, e.g. inside the 3PT line
- Play the same game dribbling
- Only dribble with the left hand

### STAFF ROLE

- Time each round on stopwatch.
- Tell the players what team wins each round.
- Make sure taggers hi-five their teammates before they start running out.

### SCORING

Team with the fastest time wins

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you be a great teammate on the sideline to support your team?"

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing agility
- Competing in teams
- Developing ball manipulation skills

MODULE 3: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-2 AROUND THE CONE

16 MIN BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 cone and 1 ball per half-court

### DESCRIPTION

An offense and a defense will start underneath the rim facing the half-court line, with the offense first and in possession of the ball, and the defender standing behind. Another offensive player will stand in the right corner, with a help defender positioned appropriately. Offense can start at any moment by dribbling around the cone on the left wing. The defender must trail, creating an advantage situation for a live 2-on-2.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Driving and kicking decision-making
- Converting advantages
- Defense recovering back to neutral

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add a second cone three big steps behind the first cone. The defense must run around the second cone, while the offense dribbles around the first. This increases the advantage.
- Change the location of the second offensive players every repetition.
- Have players complete three repetitions in a row before changing roles.
- Add an extra offensive and defensive player so it is 3-on-3.
- Add an extra cone, players can choose what side they dribble to. Other offensive players must start in 'bad spacing' and find a good spacing location to re-space to as the dribble starts.

### STAFF ROLE

- Place the cones on the wing.
- Encourage quick rotations to save time.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "When is a good time to pass the ball to your teammate?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

I-ON-2 CONVERSION INTO 2-ON-1 BACK

12 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players will be divided into groups of three. The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Cones may be used to mark out the rim line. One player will start on the baseline with a ball facing half-court. One defender will guard the ball-handler from the baseline to the free-throw line, and another defender will play defense between the free-throw line and half-court line. The offensive player must attempt to dribble to the half-court line to score a 'touchdown' within 10 seconds, without losing possession of the ball. The defenders can only stay in their areas. If the offense scores a 'touchdown' or the defense forces a turnover (steal, out of bounds, time limit), it changes to a 2-on-1 at the same basket (with offense and the defense switching roles). Ensure only two groups play on one basket at a time.

### SCORING

The ball-handler will get 3 points for successfully completing a touchdown. In the 2-on-1, the offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Handling pressure
- Disruptive defense

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders can only use one hand to defend.
- Remove the first defender's space limitations while keeping the second defender's limitations.
- Add another offensive player so that it is 2-on-2.
- Add in the 'rugby' load where offensive players can only pass laterally or backwards.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the space?"
- "What is the best shot to obtain within the 2-on-1?"

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players stay in their respective areas.
- Count down from 10 seconds.
